name: find-coverage-1.0.0
measures: atlas/pipeline/rag/find-queries.json (find-queries-1.0.0), 120 queries, against the search that ships today
fidelity: TITLE: SUGGEST_ORDER is rebuilt from corpus.json edges exactly as template.html:2798 builds it (wallBand, CLAIM_SCORE, BEST_BOND, dealHash, HEAD_RANK). The list is cut to 4, not 6, because findOfferRow returns a row for every query of 3+ characters and search() slices to 4 when it does.
LOOKUP: lookupNorm / lookupIndex / lookupFilms / lookupMatches are transcribed from template.html:9531-9600 and read pipeline/out/lookup.json, the same file build.js packs.

LOCAL: app/query-runtime.js is required directly — the page inlines this exact source. The alias path is pointed at a file that does not exist, because build.js ships only consensus-vocab, query-lexicon and questioner-phrasings to the browser's virtual filesystem, so the shipped buildTitleIndex runs with aliases={}. localWithAliases re-runs every query with the real file to price that gap.
NOT RUN: /api/interpret. It needs a model call per query and it fires only when the local reading is empty, so what is reported is its trigger rate, which is a property of the local channel.
NOT RUN: the layout. Whether a set of films is drawn well is layout-match.js's business; this measures what reaches it.

definitions.answered: the channel returned at least one film
definitions.hit: at least one of the query's named films is in the answer
definitions.good: at least ceil(n/2) of the query's named films are in the answer. For answerShape 'none' both are inverted — silence is the right answer.
definitions.lookup top-10: there is none. lookupRun draws the whole set at the centre with score 1, so a lookup answer is scored on membership and its size is reported alongside.
definitions.alphabet: all ten films in the local top 10 carry the same score, so match.js:648 `scores[b]-scores[a] || a.localeCompare(b)` ordered them by name
definitions.fragment: drawable, the reading covers under 35% of the typed characters, and no expected film landed
definitions.substring: the lookup answer came from the CONTAINED stage and no expected film landed
definitions.falseAnswer: answerShape is 'none' and some channel answered anyway

aliasDelta.what: queries whose local reading changes if film-aliases.json were shipped to the browser

queries.q: ok so I'm trying to remember a film I saw maybe fifteen years ago, it was European I think, possibly French or maybe Italian, and there's a woman who goes to an island with some friends and then she just disappears halfway through and the film sort of forgets about her and follows the others instead, which annoyed me at the time but I've thought about it ever since

my dad keeps going on about some old black and white movie he watched as a kid where a guy comes back from the war and can't settle back into normal life, everyone around him has moved on and got jobs and married and he just can't do it, and apparently there's a scene near the end in a field or a station that he says he's never forgotten, any idea what that could be

looking for something to put on tonight, nothing too heavy because it's been a long week, but also not stupid, ideally something beautiful to look at with not much plot, maybe subtitles are fine, something where you can just sort of let it wash over you and not have to concentrate too hard, and preferably not three hours long because I will fall asleep

queries.q: I want something like the feeling of the end of a long summer when you know everyone is about to go away and nothing will be the same again, not necessarily a summer film literally, more that specific ache, I don't care what country or what year, it can be sad but it shouldn't be brutal, and it should feel like it means it rather than being clever about it
